messages:
Talia Benson: Hey folks — want to nail down go/no-go criteria for incident bot collectors GA this week, plus rollback + comms plan. @Sean Gallagher @Rafael Mendes can we align here so I can draft the #eng + #incidents announcement?

Sean Gallagher: +1. Let’s decide what “GA” actually means: default-on in #incidents + enabled for all on-call rotations unless explicitly opted out? Or still behind per-channel flags but broadly recommended.

Rafael Mendes: My vote: GA = enabled by default in #incidents, with allowlist for any restricted incidents going to #incidents-private only. Still keep feature flags per collector + per channel (kill switch stays).

Aisha Bello: For go/no-go I want explicit SLO-ish targets for the bot itself, otherwise we’ll take on new pager noise. Proposed hard gates:
- bot post success rate >= 99% over 7 days
- p95 end-to-end bundle assembly < 8s (from incident created -> first bundle post)
- collector timeouts not exceeding 3s each (deploy/config/sat) w/ partial render
- < 1 “bad redaction” incident (P0) obviously (should be zero)

Jacob Stein: For latency: current p95 is ~6.2s in beta for full bundle when metrics backend is healthy; when metrics lag we render partial in ~3.5s and show “sat collector delayed”. If we treat that as success, we’re fine.

Miles Thornton: Can we add multi-region correctness gate? Specifically: deploy + config context must be region-aware and not misleading. I’ve seen a couple beta threads where it picked “latest global deploy” instead of region-specific.

Rafael Mendes: Yep, that’s still a footgun. We fixed region scoping in the deploy collector last week, but I want a validation checklist:
- for each of us-east / us-west / eu-central: trigger synthetic incident -> confirm it shows deploys/configs for that region
- if region unknown, bot says “region not detected” and posts only global links (no guesses)

Priya Natarajan: For config snapshot endpoint, we’re good on region-aware “effective config” now. One caveat: the snapshot is eventually consistent within ~60s during large rollouts. Bot should include “as of” timestamp and not claim it’s exact current state.

Sean Gallagher: Agree. “As of <ts>” is required in GA, otherwise responders assume it’s live.

Allison Grant: Observability angle: saturation collector is the one that tends to cause confusion if dashboards don’t match what it posts. I want a gate that the canonical saturation dashboards + alerts are live and validated in at least 2 real incidents or 2 game-day scenarios.

Logan Wright: Dashboard side is shipped; we still have some missing labels for a couple model pools in eu-central, but that shouldn’t block GA of deploy/config collectors. If we GA everything at once, then I’d like a carveout: saturation collector can be GA but default disabled for eu-central until label coverage is fixed.

Aisha Bello: +1 to region-specific enablement. Also: adoption / usefulness metric gate? If it’s GA and no one uses it, we’re just spamming.

Rafael Mendes: We can do a soft gate: at least 10 incident threads in beta where responders marked it “useful” (emoji or /bot feedback) and < 3 “noise/incorrect” reports. Not a perfect metric but enough.

Sean Gallagher: We should define what counts as “incorrect.” Example: suspected change heuristic overclaiming. That one makes me nervous.

Jacob Stein: We can keep “suspected change” heuristic behind a separate flag and not GA it yet. GA the context bundles (deploy/config/sat) but keep suspected-change beta-only.

Miles Thornton: Please. Any heuristic that asserts causality is risky. Better to present overlap as “recent changes around start time” without highlighting a single culprit.

Marcus Lin: Security gates:
- restricted-mode posting must be on by default for incidents tagged customer-sensitive (whatever tag we use)
- redaction audit log enabled + retention configured (at least 30d)
- config diff allowlist reviewed/approved (I’m fine with the current allowlist + denylist, but want a final pass before GA)
Also want explicit “if redaction fails closed vs open” behavior documented.

Rafael Mendes: Current behavior: if redaction step errors, we drop the config diff section and show “config diff unavailable (redaction error)” rather than posting raw. That’s effectively fail-closed for the sensitive section. Everything else fails open.

Sean Gallagher: Perfect. Make that a GA gate + mention in rollout notes.

Talia Benson: Let me summarize proposed go/no-go criteria. Tell me if I missed anything:
1) Reliability: 7-day bot post success >=99%, bot p95 bundle time <8s
2) Partial bundles render with clear per-collector errors (no silent missing)
3) Security: restricted-mode default for sensitive incidents, redaction allowlist sign-off, redaction failures do NOT leak raw data, audit logs enabled
4) Correctness: region-scoped deploy+config; unknown region -> no guessing; all sections include “as of” timestamps
5) Observability readiness: canonical dashboards/links valid; saturation collector can be region-gated if metrics labels incomplete
6) Feature flags: per-channel/per-collector kill switch tested
7) Comms/runbooks: #incidents usage guidance + “report issues” path + updated on-call docs

Aisha Bello: Add one more: bot error rate should not page on-call. Alerts should go to #eng-sre-bots or similar, with paging only if it impacts incident flow (e.g., spam / rate limit issues).

Sean Gallagher: +1, bot health alerts should be non-paging initially; we can revisit.

Logan Wright: And add cardinality guardrail check for saturation metrics before enabling saturation collector broadly. We had a near-miss on high-card labels.

Allison Grant: Yep. Gate = “no new high-cardinality label explosions” verified via 24h dry run.

Rafael Mendes: Rollback plan: keep it simple and explicit:
- global kill switch: `INCIDENT_BOT_ENABLED=false` (stops all posting)
- per-collector toggles: `COLLECTOR_DEPLOY|CONFIG|SAT_ENABLED`
- per-channel allowlist config revert to beta-only channels
- restricted-mode always stays on (do NOT roll back restricted-mode)
- if rollout causes noise: reduce posting frequency (rate limit) + disable sat collector first

Sean Gallagher: Also a responder-friendly “stop posting in this incident” command. Do we have that? If not, not a GA blocker but would be nice.

Jacob Stein: We have `/incidentbot mute` behind admin permission. It mutes for that incident thread only (stores in cache for 24h). It’s documented in the draft responder docs but not widely known.

Talia Benson: Great, I’ll include that in comms.

Miles Thornton: On rollback criteria: define triggers.
- bot posts incorrect region info in a live SEV -> immediate disable deploy/config collectors until fixed
- any redaction issue -> immediate disable config collector + security review
- if bot causes >5 extra messages per incident (spam) -> disable formatting variant + tighten rate limit

Marcus Lin: +1. Redaction issue = immediate config collector off + incident response, no debate.

Aisha Bello: For go/no-go meeting, who’s the final decision maker? Sean as incident workflow owner + Rafael as delivery lead? I can provide the metrics readout.

Sean Gallagher: I’ll own the go/no-go call, with Rafael + Marcus as required sign-offs. Aisha supplies metrics; Logan/Allison sign off on saturation dashboards; Priya signs off on config snapshot correctness.

Priya Natarajan: Works for me. One ask: in comms, please be clear that config diffs are allowlisted keys only, so people don’t assume it’s exhaustive.

Rafael Mendes: Comms plan (draft):
- Post in #eng 24h before enabling: what’s changing, how to opt out, link to docs, where to report issues
- Post in #incidents right when enabled: short “incident bot context bundles GA; here’s what you’ll see; use /incidentbot feedback or react :+1: / :no_entry_sign: to rate usefulness”
- Add pinned message in #incidents for 1 week w/ quick FAQ

Sean Gallagher: Include “If you see wrong info, say so in-thread and tag @eng-sre” so we catch it fast.

Allison Grant: And include the dashboard links are canonical; if links are broken, report in #eng-observability.

Talia Benson: Timeline: propose go/no-go tomorrow 10:30 PT (15 min). If go, enable deploy+config collectors GA same day, saturation collector GA next week after eu-central labels fixed + 24h dry run. Everyone ok?

Logan Wright: 👍 for splitting saturation rollout.

Aisha Bello: 👍

Marcus Lin: 👍 as long as I get the final allowlist diff today.

Jacob Stein: I’ll send the allowlist + current redaction tests output in this thread in ~1h.

Rafael Mendes: I’ll run the kill switch test in staging + post screenshot/log excerpt here. Also will confirm `/incidentbot mute` works as expected.

Sean Gallagher: Great. Talia, once you draft comms, drop here for quick review before posting.

Talia Benson: Will do. Thanks all.
